mark_split.label: Identify the reciprocal equation and divide by x²

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.20 — LAQ chapter 2 Theory of Equations, answer 10. Printed appearances: AP 18 · TS 15, 22. THE MARK SPLIT IS THE BOOK'S: the page prints [1 Mark] [1 Mark] [1 Mark] [2 Marks] [2 Marks] against the five stages (divide by x² · substitute · solve for t · t = 4 · t = 6) and the card follows it exactly. The SAME step ids (s1_identify, s2_substitute, s3_solve_t, s4_first_t, s5_second_t) and the same 1+1+1+2+2 shape are used on answers 10, 11 and 12, deliberately: they are one method — divide by x², put x + 1/x = t — over different numbers. The book writes the substitution letter as y; the card writes t, the letter the Telugu Akademi textbook uses. The book's chapter header carries ★★★; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. Paper position: Maths-2A Section C runs Q18–Q24 at 7 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q19 is the Theory of Equations slot (blueprint, book p.3; all five model papers pp.111–120 agree). Model Paper 1 Q19 (book p.112) is this question; the Bullet Model Paper re-solves it under Q19 on book p.105 — arithmetic cross-checked, identical. Truth check: the four roots multiply to (4 − 3)(9 − 8) = 1, the constant term, and add to 10, the negative of the x³ coefficient. Correction to the book: none. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this reciprocal equation — what you divide by, what you substitute, and how each value of t gives two roots.
insider_note: Most students lose the −2 in x² + 1/x² = t² − 2; write the squaring line and the two 2-mark endings follow.

steps.label: Reciprocal form
steps.margin_note: First mark. Read the coefficients from both ends: 1, −10, 26, −10, 1. Same both ways, degree even — a standard reciprocal equation. Divide by x² and pair each term with its matching term from the other end.
lines: Degree n = 4 is even, and aₖ = aₙ₋ₖ for every k
So this is a standard reciprocal equation.
x ≠ 0, so divide every term by x²:

recall.must_convey: That the degree is even and the coefficients 1, −10, 26, −10, 1 read the same from both ends, so the equation is a standard reciprocal equation, and that dividing by x² lets the terms be grouped in pairs.
accept: the degree is even and the coefficients are the same from both ends so it is a standard reciprocal equation, divide by x square and group the terms
coefficients read the same forwards and backwards so divide through by x squared and pair x squared with one by x squared
identify it as a reciprocal equation and divide by x square
coefficients rendu vaipula same, kabatti reciprocal equation, x square tho divide chesi group cheyyali
it is reciprocal because a k equals a n minus k, so divide every term by x squared
heard_as: a k equals a n minus k

steps.why: A standard reciprocal equation of even degree 2m can always be cut to a degree-m equation in t = x + 1/x, because dividing by xᵐ pairs each term with its matching term from the other end. Checking the symmetry first is what earns the right to that shortcut.
common_mistakes: Dividing by x² but writing the terms in the wrong pairs (x² must pair with 1/x², x with 1/x).
Calling every symmetric-looking equation reciprocal without checking every coefficient pair.
Forgetting to note x ≠ 0 before dividing (0 is not a root, since the constant term is not 0).

steps.label: Put x + 1/x = t
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The whole method is the identity x² + 1/x² = t² − 2. Write the squaring line once so the −2 is visible, then the equation is a quadratic in t.

recall.must_convey: That x + 1/x is replaced by t, and that x² + 1/x² is then t² − 2 (from squaring), which turns the equation into a quadratic in t.
accept: put x plus one by x equal to t so x squared plus one by x squared is t squared minus two and the equation becomes a quadratic in t
substitute t for x plus one over x and use t squared minus two for the squared pair
let x plus one by x be t, square it, and the pair of squares is t square minus two
x plus one by x ni t ga pettali, x square plus one by x square ante t square minus two
the substitution is t equals x plus its reciprocal, and the squared pair is t squared minus two

steps.why: x² + 1/x² is NOT t²; squaring t = x + 1/x gives t² = x² + 2 + 1/x², so the pair of squares is t² − 2. This one identity is the whole method — every mark after it depends on the −2 being there.
common_mistakes: Writing x² + 1/x² = t² and losing the −2.
Substituting for x + 1/x but leaving x² + 1/x² unchanged.

steps.label: Solve for t
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Split the middle term: −10 = −6 − 4 with (−6)(−4) = 24. Two values of t, so four roots are coming.

recall.must_convey: That the quadratic in t is factorised (or solved) to give the two values of t.
accept: factorise the quadratic in t and get the two values of t
solve the t equation by splitting the middle term
the quadratic in t factors and gives two t values
t quadratic ni factorise chesi rendu t values teeskovali
split the middle term of the t equation and read off t

steps.why: The t-equation is a plain quadratic, so factorising it is the cheapest way to the two values of t. Each t value will give two x values, so the count of roots (2 × 2 = 4) is checked here before any x is found.
common_mistakes: A sign slip when splitting the middle term.
Stopping at the two t values as if they were the roots.
Solving the t-quadratic with the formula and making an arithmetic slip a factorisation would have avoided.

steps.label: t = 4
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Multiply x + 1/x = 4 by x to get x² − 4x + 1 = 0. The discriminant 16 − 4 = 12 = 4 × 3, so √12 = 2√3 and the 2 cancels with the denominator.

recall.must_convey: That t = 4 is put back into x + 1/x = t, multiplied out to a quadratic in x, and solved to give the roots 2 ± √3.
accept: put t equals 4 back so x plus one by x is 4 multiply by x to get a quadratic and solve it
x plus one over x equals 4 gives a quadratic in x whose roots are 2 ± √3
go back from t equals 4 to a quadratic in x and solve
t equals 4 ni tirigi x plus one by x lo petti quadratic solve cheyyali
multiply x plus one by x equals 4 through by x and use the quadratic formula

steps.why: Each value of t gives two values of x, because x + 1/x = t is a quadratic in x. Solving both t values is what recovers all 4 roots of the original equation — stopping at t answers a different question.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply through by x, so the equation in x is never formed.
A slip inside the square root: 16 − 4 = 12, and √12 = 2√3.
Not simplifying the surd form of the roots at the end.

steps.label: t = 6
steps.margin_note: Last two marks. x² − 6x + 1 = 0 has discriminant 36 − 4 = 32 = 16 × 2, so √32 = 4√2. Box all four roots together; a check is that their product is 1, the constant term.

recall.must_convey: That t = 6 is put back into x + 1/x = t, multiplied out to a quadratic in x, and solved to give the roots 3 ± 2√2.
accept: put t equals 6 back so x plus one by x is 6 multiply by x to get a quadratic and solve it
x plus one over x equals 6 gives a quadratic in x whose roots are 3 ± 2√2
go back from t equals 6 to a quadratic in x and solve
t equals 6 ni tirigi x plus one by x lo petti quadratic solve cheyyali
multiply x plus one by x equals 6 through by x and use the quadratic formula
